name: PixMapr Lite – Interactive Image Hotspots
author: Walter Pinem

sections.description:
PixMapr Lite turns a static image into something visitors use. Draw polygon, circle, or rectangle hotspots straight on the picture, give each one a title, text, an image, or a link, and embed the result anywhere with the PixMapr block or the [pixmapr] shortcode.

No coordinates to type, no external service, no account. Everything is drawn and stored on your own site.

Free, and enough for real work:

  • Unlimited interactive images — no cap, no counter.
  • Unlimited hotspots per image – polygon, circle, and rectangle, traced on the image itself.
  • Two layouts – an info panel beside the image, or a tooltip that follows the hotspot.
  • Click or hover to open a hotspot.
  • Info panels and links – a title, rich text, and an image per hotspot, or send visitors to any URL.
  • Five color themes – Light, Dark, PixMapr, Suzette, and Autumn.
  • A panel that widens: a tab on the info panel widens it over the image, so videos, audio, and long reads get room.
  • Markers your way: dots that can pulse, or an emoji or image of a hotspot’s own.
  • Previous and Next buttons that step through the hotspots like a guided tour.
  • A sample to start from: one click makes a ready-made interactive image to explore.
  • Phone-friendly – a tappable hotspot list replaces hard-to-hit shapes on small screens.
  • Accessible – keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, and screen reader announcements out of the box.
  • Block and shortcode – works in the block editor, the Classic Editor, Divi, and any builder that renders shortcodes.
  • Light on the page – serve a smaller image size than the original and lazy-load images near the viewport.
  • Your own themes – five ready-made palettes, a theme builder for your own, and alternate highlight styles per image.
  • Translation-ready and RTL-ready.

What could you make?

  • A floor plan where every room opens its photo and description.
  • A product photo where each part explains itself.
  • An annotated map, chart, or infographic.
  • A team photo that links each face to a profile.
  • A modern replacement for an HTML image map that works on phones.

PixMapr Pro

PixMapr Pro is the full plugin, built and used by the people who run the Online Store Kit stores:

  • Unlimited interactive images
  • Six layouts: left, right, top, bottom, lightbox, and tooltip
  • Numbered markers with a matching legend
  • Pan, zoom, and fullscreen for large maps and floor plans, with a separate phone layout
  • WooCommerce hotspots: tag products and sell from the picture, with add to cart that works without a page reload
  • 20+ themes
  • Engagement counts – image views and hotspot opens, counts only, no personal data
  • Export and import images, themes, and settings as one file
  • Ten automatic snapshots of every image, and one-click duplicate
  • Elementor widget and Beaver Builder module
  • A year of signed automatic updates and email support

Pro and Lite share the same images, so upgrading is install-and-activate: nothing to migrate, nothing to redraw. Lite can even stay active alongside Pro.

Privacy

PixMapr Lite does not call any external service and stores no visitor data. The only outbound links are the ones in its own admin screens.

Credits

Drawing and rendering are built on three bundled open-source libraries:

  • Leaflet 1.9.4 — BSD-2-Clause
  • Leaflet.draw 1.0.4 — MIT
  • leaflet-responsive-popup 1.0.0 — BSD-2-Clause

Full copyright notices and licence texts ship with the plugin in
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt. Un-minified sources for all three are in
assets/src/ and from the upstream projects above.
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins → Add New and search for “PixMapr”.
  2. Install and activate PixMapr Lite.
  3. Go to PixMapr → Add New, choose an image, and draw your first hotspot.
  4. Add the PixMapr block to any page or post, or paste the [pixmapr id="123"] shortcode shown on the edit screen.

Manual install

  1. Upload the pixmapr-lite folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin from the Plugins screen.
sections.faq:
What is the difference between Lite and Pro?

Lite builds unlimited interactive images with unlimited hotspots, two layouts (info panel and tooltip), five themes, and hotspots that open an info panel or a link — with no cap on any of it.

Pro is a bigger plugin: four more layouts including a lightbox, numbered markers with a matching legend, pan/zoom/fullscreen, WooCommerce product hotspots, fifteen more themes, engagement counts, export/import, snapshots, and the Elementor and Beaver Builder integrations. Compare the two.

Is there a limit on how many images I can make?

No. Build as many interactive images as you like, with as many hotspots on each as you like.

Do I need to uninstall Lite to use Pro?

No. Install Pro and Lite steps aside automatically. Both plugins use the same images, so everything you drew is already there.

Does it work in Elementor, Divi, or the Classic Editor?

The [pixmapr] shortcode works in any editor or builder that renders shortcodes, including Elementor, Divi, and the Classic Editor. The block editor gets a dedicated PixMapr block. A native Elementor widget and Beaver Builder module are part of Pro.

Does it work on phones?

Yes. The info panel and tooltip layouts adapt to small screens, and a tappable hotspot list can replace shapes that are too small to hit with a finger.

Is it accessible?

Yes. Hotspots can be reached and opened with the keyboard, carry ARIA labels, and info panels announce their content to screen readers.

Where do I get help?

Post in the support forum. The documentation covers both editions.

Where do I report a security issue?

Please use the contact form rather than the public forum, so it can be fixed before it is disclosed.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • New: Start from a sample. The first-run screen and the images list can create a ready-made interactive image, a map of Tokyo with six neighbourhoods, to explore and change.
  • New: each hotspot can have its own marker: an emoji or an image, with its own color and size. A hotspot with its own icon or image shows it even when the image has markers turned off.
  • New: Previous and Next buttons step through an image’s hotspots in order, in the information box and click tooltips. Turn them on site-wide in Settings, per image, or in the block and the shortcode (tour).
  • New: markers can pulse, so visitors see at a glance that the image has more to show (marker_animation). They stay still for visitors whose device asks for reduced motion.
  • New: a link button on each hotspot in the editor copies an address that opens the image with that hotspot already open.
  • New: Copy style and Paste style on each hotspot give several hotspots the same highlight style and marker.
  • New: hotspots that go to a web address can be marked Nofollow, or Sponsored for paid and affiliate links.
  • New: move a hotspot’s shape a pixel at a time with the arrow keys, ten with Shift.
  • New: the image editor warns before you leave it with unsaved changes.
  • New: after two weeks of use and a first published image, a notice on PixMapr screens asks administrators once whether they would rate the plugin on WordPress.org. Maybe later and Don’t ask again both work.
  • New: the information box beside the image can widen over it like a sidebar sliding out, so videos, audio and long descriptions get room. A tab on its edge, or the Esc key, widens and narrows it.
  • New: settings for the widening box, site-wide and per image: whether the tab shows, how far the box widens (40% to 100% of the image), and whether it widens by itself for videos, audio and embeds, or for every hotspot. The block and the shortcode have them too (expand, expand_width, expand_auto).
  • Improved: scrollbars in the information box and tooltips are thin and take the box’s own colors, so they match every theme.
  • Improved: the block editor preview no longer shows the phone-only hotspot list under the image.
  • Improved: tooltips long enough to scroll no longer show grey lines above and below the text.
  • Fixed: Open in New Window on hotspots that go to a web address opened the link in the same tab.
  • Fixed: a link to a hotspot now opens it on images that open hotspots on hover.
  • Fixed: clicks inside a tooltip now reach the page’s own scripts, so buttons and links in a tooltip work as they do elsewhere on the page.
  • Fixed: opening an Elementor popup on a page with an image restarted that image, and its information box showed the introduction on top of the open hotspot.
  • Fixed: in themes that wrap videos in a frame of their own (Kadence, FitVids), videos in the information box were taller than the video, with an empty band above it.
  • Fixed: a color or other value that a hotspot field rejected was saved anyway.

1.0.2

  • Fixed: the background color around an image is now even on all four sides. When the page layout settled after loading, for example once a web font arrived, the image could end up with no border at the top and a thick one at the bottom.
  • Fixed: tooltips now open beside the hotspot’s marker instead of covering it.
  • Fixed: the hotspot editor no longer leaves an empty space on the left of each hotspot.

1.0.1

  • Fixed: tooltips could stop opening on pages where the theme or another plugin loads its own copy of the Leaflet map library. PixMapr now keeps working whichever copy loads last.
  • Fixed: lists, headings and paragraphs in a hotspot description now keep their formatting in the tooltip layout. Bullets and numbers show on every theme, and the tooltip uses the site’s own typeface at a readable size.
  • Fixed: the hotspot list no longer picks up a theme’s bullets and indent.
  • Improved: uploading a map image now shows a spinner with progress, and says when the image is being processed. A large image no longer looks as if nothing is happening.
  • Fixed: after uploading a map image and then removing it, the upload box could stay empty until the page was reloaded.
  • Improved: a file that is too large, of the wrong type, or refused by the server now says so in the Map Image box.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.

short_description: Turn any image into clickable hotspots. Unlimited images and hotspots, keyboard accessible, embedded with a block or shortcode.
